    CHAPTER I

The motor-car stood waiting at the gate, and the driver leaned
against the door with his cap pushed back upon his head. He had
been waiting there since noon, and he was weary of it.

A motorcar is a costly thing to keep, and the old man grumbled
about the price of it whenever the subject came up at dinner.

The school-house on the hill was empty now, and no one had come
to open it since the summer began. Nobody spoke of the schoolhouse
any more, though it had once been the pride of the parish.

Her sister-in-law came down from the city every summer, and she
brought with her a trunk of books and a great deal of advice
which nobody in the house had asked for.
